why: I checked every command in both briefs. The builder's `npm test` runs, and so do the commands for Checks 1, 2 and 4. Check 3 breaks. It is wrapped in bash double quotes, where `\\` becomes `\`. So JavaScript gets `'^#+ .*\b'+n+'\s*\('`. Inside a JS string literal, `\b` is a backspace character, `\s` becomes `s` and `\(` becomes `(`. The pattern passed to `new RegExp` ends in `s*(`, an unterminated group. That throws a SyntaxError on the first exported name. So Check 3 cannot print PASS for any README, even a correct one. Getting a regex escape through both the shell and a JS string needs `\\\\b`, `\\\\s` and `\\\\(`, or single-quoted shell. As written, this command is broken.
